Assignment 2: Hand Gesture Recognition [50 Pt]¶

This assignment will be completed in two parts. In Part A you will gain experience gathering your own data set (specifically images of hand gestures), and understand the challenges involved in the data cleaning process. In Part B you will train a convolutional neural network to make classifications on different hand gestures. By the end of this assignment, you should be able to:

  1. Generate and preprocess your own data
  2. Load and split data for training, validation and testing
  3. Train a Convolutional Neural Network
  4. Apply transfer learning to improve your model

Note that for this assignment we will not be providing you with any starter code. You should be able to take the sample code provided in the preparation sample code, previous assignment, and lectures and modify it accordingly to complete the tasks outlined below.

This assignment is based on an assignment developed by Prof. Lisa Zhang.

Individual image file names should follow the convention of student-number_Alphabet_file-number.jpg (e.g. 100343434_A_1.jpg).

Part A. Data Collection [5pt]¶

So far, we have worked with data sets that have been collected, cleaned, and curated by machine learning researchers and practitioners. Datasets like MNIST and CIFAR are often used as toy examples, both by students and by researchers testing new machine learning models.

In the real world, getting a clean data set is never that easy. More than half the work in applying machine learning is finding, gathering, cleaning, and formatting your data set.

The purpose of this assignment is to help you gain experience gathering your own data set, and understand the challenges involved in the data cleaning process.

American Sign Language¶

American Sign Language (ASL) is a complete, complex language that employs signs made by moving the hands combined with facial expressions and postures of the body. It is the primary language of many North Americans who are deaf and is one of several communication options used by people who are deaf or hard-of-hearing.

The hand gestures representing English alphabet are shown below. This assignment focuses on classifying a subset of these hand gesture images using convolutional neural networks. Specifically, given an image of a hand showing one of the letters A-I, we want to detect which letter is being represented.

Generating Data¶

We will produce the images required to assess our models by ourselves. You are required to collect, clean and submit three images each of Americal Sign Language gestures for letters A - I (total of 27 images) Steps involved in data collection

  1. Familiarize yourself with American Sign Language gestures for letters from A - I (9 letters).
  2. Take three pictures at slightly different orientation for each letter gesture using your mobile phone.
  • Ensure adequate lighting while you are capturing the images.
  • Use a white wall as your background.
  • Use your right hand to create gestures (for consistency).
  • Keep your right hand fairly apart from your body and any other obstructions.
  • Avoid having shadows on parts of your hand.
  1. Transfer the images to your laptop for cleaning.

Cleaning Data¶

To simplify the machine learning the task, we will standardize the training images. We will make sure that all our images are of the same size (224 x 224 pixels RGB), and have the hand in the center of the cropped regions.

You may use the following applications to crop and resize your images:

Mac

  • Use Preview: – Holding down CMD + Shift will keep a square aspect ratio while selecting the hand area. – Resize to 224x224 pixels.

Windows 10

  • Use Photos app to edit and crop the image and keep the aspect ratio a square.
  • Use Paint to resize the image to the final image size of 224x224 pixels.

Linux

  • You can use GIMP, imagemagick, or other tools of your choosing. You may also use online tools such as http://picresize.com All the above steps are illustrative only. You need not follow these steps but following these will ensure that you produce a good quality dataset. You will be judged based on the quality of the images alone. Please do not edit your photos in any other way. You should not need to change the aspect ratio of your image. You also should not digitally remove the background or shadows—instead, take photos with a white background and minimal shadows.

Accepted Images¶

Images will be accepted and graded based on the criteria below

  1. The final image should be size 224x224 pixels (RGB).
  2. The file format should be a .jpg file.
  3. The hand should be approximately centered on the frame.
  4. The hand should not be obscured or cut off.
  5. The photos follows the ASL gestures posted earlier.
  6. The photos were not edited in any other way (e.g. no electronic removal of shadows or background).

Submission¶

Submit a zip file containing your images. There should be a total of 27 images (3 for each category)

  2. Zip all the images together and name it with the following convention: last-name_student-number.zip (e.g. last-name_100343434.zip).
  3. Submit the zipped folder.

# ======== part 3: Transfiormation ========

class ASLDataset(Dataset):
    def __init__(self, samples, classes, class_to_idx, img_size=224):
        self.samples = [(p, class_to_idx[c]) for p, c in samples]
        self.num_classes = len(class_to_idx)
        self.classes = classes
        self.img_size = img_size

    def __len__(self):
        return len(self.samples)

    def __getitem__(self, i):
        path, y_idx = self.samples[i]
        arr = plt.imread(str(path))                 # (224,224,3)
        if arr.ndim == 2:                           # grey handling
            arr = np.stack([arr] * 3, axis=-1)
        if arr.dtype != np.float32:
            arr = arr.astype(np.float32) / (255.0 if arr.max() > 1.0 else 1.0)

        # resize to 224×224
        img = Image.fromarray((arr * 255).astype(np.uint8))
        img = img.resize((self.img_size, self.img_size), Image.BILINEAR)
        arr = np.asarray(img).astype(np.float32) / 255.0

        x = torch.from_numpy(arr.transpose(2, 0, 1))  # -> (3,224,224), [0,1]

        # one-hot encoding of y
        y = torch.zeros(self.num_classes, dtype=torch.float32)
        y[y_idx] = 1.0
        return x, y



# ======== part 4: Split Data ========

def get_loaders_split_by_person(samples, class_to_idx, batch_size=64,
                                seed=seed, val_ratio=0.2, test_ratio=0.15,
                                shuffle_train=True):
    """
    Split into Train/Val/Test by person ID (filename prefix before the first underscore),
    and return DataLoaders.

    Args:
        samples: list of (Path, class_name)
        class_to_idx: dict {class_name: class_idx}
        batch_size: DataLoader batch size
        seed: RNG seed
        val_ratio: fraction of UNIQUE persons assigned to validation
        test_ratio: fraction of UNIQUE persons assigned to test
        shuffle_train: whether to shuffle the training DataLoader

    Returns:
        train_loader, val_loader, test_loader, split_meta (dict)
    """

    # 1) Derive person IDs from filenames: "<personID>_<class>_<sampleID>.jpg"
    persons = np.array([p.name.split('_', 1)[0] for p, _ in samples])
    uniq = np.unique(persons)


    # 2) Person-level split (disjoint persons across splits)
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    perm = rng.permutation(len(uniq))

    n_test = int(test_ratio * len(uniq))                          # 15% test data
    n_val  = int((1 - test_ratio) * val_ratio * len(uniq))        # 17% validation data (i.e. (1-0.15) * 0.2 = 0.17)
                                                                  # 68% training data
    test_persons = set(uniq[perm[:n_test]])
    val_persons  = set(uniq[perm[n_test:n_test + n_val]])
    train_persons = set(uniq[perm[n_test + n_val:]])

    idx = np.arange(len(samples))
    train_idx = idx[np.isin(persons, list(train_persons))]
    val_idx   = idx[np.isin(persons, list(val_persons))]
    test_idx  = idx[np.isin(persons, list(test_persons))]


    # 3) Build Datasets and DataLoaders
    full_ds  = ASLDataset(samples, classes, class_to_idx)   # defined earlier: one-hot + plt.imread
    train_ds = Subset(full_ds, train_idx.tolist())
    val_ds   = Subset(full_ds,   val_idx.tolist())
    test_ds  = Subset(full_ds,  test_idx.tolist())


    train_loader = DataLoader(train_ds, batch_size=batch_size, shuffle=shuffle_train)
    val_loader   = DataLoader(val_ds,   batch_size=batch_size, shuffle=False)
    test_loader  = DataLoader(test_ds,  batch_size=batch_size, shuffle=False)


    # 4) Metadata for reporting/reproducibility
    split_meta = {
        "num_images": {
            "train": len(train_ds), "val": len(val_ds), "test": len(test_ds)
        },
        "num_persons": {
            "train": int(len(train_persons)), "val": int(len(val_persons)), "test": int(len(test_persons))
        },
        "ratios": {"val_ratio": val_ratio, "test_ratio": test_ratio},
        "seed": seed
    }
    return train_loader, val_loader, test_loader, split_meta




# ======== part 5: Plot Distribution of Split Datasets ========

def labels_from_subset(loader):
  '''
  Get labels from a subset for plotting distribution of classes
  '''
  base_subset = loader.dataset          # DataLoader -> Subset
  ds = base_subset.dataset              # Subset -> ASLDataset
  idxs = base_subset.indices            # idx to ds.samples
  y_idx = np.array([ds.samples[i][1] for i in idxs], dtype=int)  # class idx
  classes = np.array(ds.classes)        # class list

  return y_idx



def plot_dist(y, classes, title):
    """
    Plot distribution of classes with count labels on bars.
    """

    y = np.asarray(y)
    counts = np.bincount(y, minlength=len(classes))

    fig, ax = plt.subplots()
    ax.set_title(title)
    x = np.arange(len(classes))
    bars = ax.bar(x, counts)
    ax.set_xticks(x)
    ax.set_xticklabels(classes, rotation=45, ha='right')
    ax.set_ylabel("Example Count")
    fig.tight_layout()

    ax.bar_label(bars, padding=2)
    plt.show()
    return counts


def balance_report(counts, split_name):
  '''
  Use min/max ratio to determine if dataset is balanced or imbalanced.
  '''

  ratio = counts.max() / counts.min()
  print(f"{split_name}: min={counts.min()}, max={counts.max()}, imbalance_ratio={ratio:.2f} "
        f"-> {'Imbalanced' if ratio > 1.5 else 'Balanced-ish'}")

Part (i) Convolutional Network [2pt MODEL]¶

Build a convolutional neural network model that takes the (224x224 RGB) image as input, and predicts the gesture letter. Your model should be a subclass of nn.Module. Explain your choice of neural network architecture: how many layers did you choose? What types of layers did you use? Were they fully-connected or convolutional? What about other decisions like pooling layers, activation functions, number of channels / hidden units?

# TO BE COMPLETED

class cnn(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, num_classes=9, p=0.2):
      super(cnn, self).__init__()
      self.name = "cnn"
      self.conv1 = nn.Conv2d(3, 6, kernel_size=3, padding=0, bias=False)      # 224 -> 222 -> pool -> 111
      self.bn1 = nn.BatchNorm2d(6)
      self.conv2 = nn.Conv2d(6, 16, kernel_size=3, padding=0, bias=False)     # 111 -> 109 -> pool -> 54
      self.bn2 = nn.BatchNorm2d(16)
      self.conv3 = nn.Conv2d(16, 32, kernel_size=3, padding=0, bias=False)    # 54 -> 52 -> pool -> 26
      self.bn3 = nn.BatchNorm2d(32)
      self.conv4 = nn.Conv2d(32, 64, kernel_size=3, padding=0, bias=False)    # 26 -> 24 -> pool -> 12
      self.bn4 = nn.BatchNorm2d(64)
      self.conv5 = nn.Conv2d(64, 128, kernel_size=3, padding=0, bias=False)    # 12 -> 10 -> pool -> 5
      self.bn5 = nn.BatchNorm2d(128)
      self.pool = nn.MaxPool2d(2,2)
      self.dropout = nn.Dropout(p)
      self.fc = nn.Linear(128 * 5 * 5, num_classes)


    def forward(self, x):
      x = self.pool(F.relu(self.bn1(self.conv1(x))))
      x = self.pool(F.relu(self.bn2(self.conv2(x))))
      x = self.pool(F.relu(self.bn3(self.conv3(x))))
      x = self.pool(F.relu(self.bn4(self.conv4(x))))
      x = self.pool(F.relu(self.bn5(self.conv5(x))))
      x = x.view(-1, 128 * 5 * 5)
      logits = self.dropout(self.fc(x))

      return logits

Part (ii) Training Code [2pt MODEL]¶

Write code that trains your neural network given some training data. Your training code should make it easy to tweak the usual hyperparameters, like batch size, learning rate, and the model object itself. Make sure that you are checkpointing your models from time to time (the frequency is up to you). Explain your choice of loss function and optimizer.

In [52]:
def evaluate(net, loader, criterion, device=None):
    """Evaluate the network on a given dataset."""

    net.eval()
    if device is None:
        device = next(net.parameters()).device

    total_loss = 0.0
    total_err = 0
    total_samples = 0

    with torch.no_grad():
        for inputs, labels_onehot in loader:  # labels are one-hot from our dataset

            targets = labels_onehot.argmax(dim=1)  # one-hot -> class idx
            outputs = net(inputs)

            # Compute loss
            loss = criterion(outputs, targets)

            pred = outputs.argmax(dim=1)
            total_err += (pred != targets).sum().item()
            total_loss += loss.item()
            total_samples += targets.size(0)

    err = total_err / total_samples
    avg_loss = total_loss / max(1, len(loader))

    return err, avg_loss




def get_model_name(name, batch_size, learning_rate, epoch,
                   weight_decay, dropout_p):
    """Generate a safe checkpoint path and ensure directory exists."""

    fname = "model_{name}_bs{batch_size}_lr{learning_rate}_wd{weight_decay}_dp{dropout_p}_epoch{epoch}".format(
        name=name, batch_size=batch_size, learning_rate=learning_rate,
        weight_decay=weight_decay, dropout_p=dropout_p, epoch=epoch+1)
    return fname




def _get_num_classes(loader):
  """For handling Small datasets without all classes"""
  ds = loader.dataset

  while isinstance(ds, Subset):
      ds = ds.dataset
  if hasattr(ds, "num_classes"): return int(ds.num_classes)
  if hasattr(ds, "classes"):     return len(ds.classes)
  raise ValueError("Cannot infer num_classes from dataset.")
In [ ]:
def train_net_cnn(net, train_loader, val_loader, test_loader, seed=seed,
                  num_epochs=20, learning_rate=1e-3, weight_decay=0,
                  dp=0, batch_size=BATCH_SIZE, device=None):

    # infer classes from the given loader
    num_classes = _get_num_classes(train_loader)

    # instantiate model (if a class was passed)
    net = cnn(num_classes=num_classes, p=dp) if isinstance(net, type) else net

    # device
    if device is None:
        device = "cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu"
    net = net.to(device)
    net.train()

    torch.manual_seed(seed)
    criterion = nn.CrossEntropyLoss()
    optimizer = optim.Adam(net.parameters(), lr=learning_rate, weight_decay=weight_decay)

    train_err = np.zeros(num_epochs); train_loss = np.zeros(num_epochs)
    val_err   = np.zeros(num_epochs); val_loss   = np.zeros(num_epochs)

    t0 = time.time()
    for epoch in range(num_epochs):
        net.train()
        tot_loss, tot_err, tot_n = 0.0, 0, 0

        # training
        for x, y_onehot in train_loader:
            x = x.to(device)
            y = y_onehot.argmax(1).long().to(device)

            optimizer.zero_grad()
            logits = net(x)
            loss = criterion(logits, y)
            loss.backward()
            optimizer.step()

            pred = logits.argmax(1)
            tot_err  += (pred != y).sum().item()
            tot_loss += loss.item()
            tot_n    += y.size(0)

        train_err[epoch]  = tot_err / tot_n
        train_loss[epoch] = tot_loss / max(1, len(train_loader))

        # validation
        net.eval(); tl, te, tn = 0.0, 0, 0
        with torch.no_grad():
            for x, y_onehot in val_loader:
                x = x.to(device)
                y = y_onehot.argmax(1).long().to(device)
                out = net(x)
                l = criterion(out, y)
                p = out.argmax(1)
                te += (p != y).sum().item()
                tl += l.item()
                tn += y.size(0)
        val_err[epoch]  = te / tn
        val_loss[epoch] = tl / max(1, len(val_loader))

        print(f"Epoch {epoch+1:02d} | train err {train_err[epoch]:.4f} loss {train_loss[epoch]:.4f} || "
              f"val err {val_err[epoch]:.4f} loss {val_loss[epoch]:.4f}")

        # Save the current model (checkpoint) to a file
        model_path = get_model_name(net.name, batch_size, learning_rate, epoch, weight_decay, dp)
        torch.save(net.state_dict(), model_path)



            # Write the train/test loss/error into CSV files for plotting later
    epochs = np.arange(1, num_epochs + 1)
    np.savetxt(f"{model_path}_train_err.csv", train_err)
    np.savetxt(f"{model_path}_train_loss.csv", train_loss)
    np.savetxt(f"{model_path}_val_err.csv", val_err)
    np.savetxt(f"{model_path}_val_loss.csv", val_loss)
    print("Finished Training. Elapsed: %.1fs" % (time.time() - t0))

    return {"train_err": train_err, "train_loss": train_loss,
            "val_err": val_err, "val_loss": val_loss}

Part (iii) “Overfit” to a Small Dataset - [1pt MODEL]¶

One way to sanity check our neural network model and training code is to check whether the model is capable of “overfitting” or “memorizing” a small dataset. A properly constructed CNN with correct training code should be able to memorize the answers to a small number of images quickly.

Construct a small dataset (e.g. just the images that you have collected). Then show that your model and training code is capable of memorizing the labels of this small data set.

With a large batch size (e.g. the entire small dataset) and learning rate that is not too high, you should be able to obtain a 100% training accuracy on that small dataset relatively quickly (within 200 iterations).

In [ ]:
# TO BE COMPLETED

# =============== part 1: grab a small dataset =========

def grab_small_batch(n_img, loader):
    """Take one ready-made batch (already transformed by your dataset) from an existing loader."""

    ds = loader.dataset
    total = len(ds)
    N = min(n_img, total)
    g = torch.Generator().manual_seed(seed)

    idx = torch.randperm(total, generator=g)[:N]
    small_ds = Subset(ds, idx)
    small_loader = DataLoader(small_ds, batch_size=N, shuffle=False)
    x, y_onehot = next(iter(small_loader))

    return small_loader, idx, x, y_onehot


# =============== part 2: sanity check =========
def overfit_sanity_check(net, loader, n_img=32, max_steps=200, lr=1e-3, num_classes=9):
    """
    Overfit a tiny subset to sanity-check model & training loop.
    Assumes train_ds returns (x, one_hot_y).
    """
    if isinstance(net, type):
        net = net(num_classes=num_classes)    # initialize any skipped classes in small set

    device = "cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu"
    net = net.to(device).train()

    _, _, x, y_onehot = grab_small_batch(n_img, loader)
    x = x.to(device)
    y = y_onehot.argmax(dim=1).to(device)

    criterion = nn.CrossEntropyLoss()
    optimizer = optim.Adam(net.parameters(), lr=lr, weight_decay=0.0)

    acc = 0.0
    for _ in range(max_steps):
        optimizer.zero_grad()
        logits = net(x)
        loss = criterion(logits, y)
        loss.backward()
        optimizer.step()
        with torch.no_grad():
            acc = (logits.argmax(1) == y).float().mean().item()
        if acc == 1.0:
            print("✅ Reached 100% training accuracy on the small set.")
            break
        # else:
        #     print(f"Accuracy: {acc:.4f}")
    return acc, net, _

acc, net, _= overfit_sanity_check(cnn, train_loader)

# Training Curve

def plot_training_curve(path, model_num, return_val_error=False):
    """ Plot training and validation error/loss curves.

    Args:
        path: Base path for the CSV files containing training logs.
        return_val_error: If True, return the final validation error.
    """

    train_err = np.loadtxt(f"{path}_train_err.csv")
    val_err = np.loadtxt(f"{path}_val_err.csv")
    train_loss = np.loadtxt(f"{path}_train_loss.csv")
    val_loss = np.loadtxt(f"{path}_val_loss.csv")

    if return_val_error:
        return val_err[-1]  # Return the final validation error

    plt.figure()
    plt.title(f"Model {model_num} — Train vs Validation Error")
    plt.plot(range(1, len(train_err) + 1), train_err, label="Train")
    plt.plot(range(1, len(val_err) + 1), val_err, label="Validation")
    plt.xlabel("Epoch")
    plt.ylabel("Error")
    plt.legend(loc='best')
    plt.show()

    plt.figure()
    plt.title(f"Model {model_num} — Train vs Validation Loss")
    plt.plot(range(1, len(train_loss) + 1), train_loss, label="Train")
    plt.plot(range(1, len(val_loss) + 1), val_loss, label="Validation")
    plt.xlabel("Epoch")
    plt.ylabel("Loss")
    plt.legend(loc='best')
    plt.show()

with torch.no_grad():
  for x, y_onehot in test_loader:
    logit = net(x)    # model 6

    y_pred.append(logit.argmax(1).numpy())
    y_test.append(y_onehot.argmax(1).numpy())

y_pred = np.concatenate(y_pred)
y_test = np.concatenate(y_test)

cm = confusion_matrix(y_test, y_pred,labels=np.arange(num_classes))
print("Confusion Matrix (counts):\n", cm)

# ===================== part 3: Statistics ==================

TP =np.diag(cm)
FP = cm.sum(axis=0) - TP
TN = cm.sum(axis=1) - TP

precision = TP / (TP + FP)
recall = TN / (TP + TN)

f1 = 2 * (precision * recall) / (precision + recall)

report_df = pd.DataFrame({
    'Class': classes,
    'Precision': precision,
    'Recall': recall,
    'F1-Score': f1
})

print("\nPer-class metrics:")
display(report_df)

cm_off = cm.copy()

pairs = [((i, j), cm_off[i, j]) for i in range(num_classes) for j in range(num_classes) if i != j and cm_off[i, j] > 0]

Part 4. Transfer Learning [8pt]¶

For many image classification tasks, it is generally not a good idea to train a very large deep neural network model from scratch due to the enormous compute requirements and lack of sufficient amounts of training data.

One of the better options is to try using an existing model that performs a similar task to the one you need to solve. This method of utilizing a pre-trained network for other similar tasks is broadly termed Transfer Learning. In this assignment, we will use Transfer Learning to extract features from the hand gesture images. Then, train a smaller network to use these features as input and classify the hand gestures.

As you have learned from the CNN lecture, convolution layers extract various features from the images which get utilized by the fully connected layers for correct classification. AlexNet architecture played a pivotal role in establishing Deep Neural Nets as a go-to tool for image classification problems and we will use an ImageNet pre-trained AlexNet model to extract features in this assignment.

Part (i) - [2pt EXPLORATORY]¶

Here is the code to load the AlexNet network, with pretrained weights. When you first run the code, PyTorch will download the pretrained weights from the internet.

In [ ]:
import torchvision.models
alexnet = torchvision.models.alexnet(pretrained=True)

The current behavior is equivalent to passing `weights=AlexNet_Weights.IMAGENET1K_V1`. You can also use `weights=AlexNet_Weights.DEFAULT` to get the most up-to-date weights.

100%|██████████| 233M/233M [00:03<00:00, 72.1MB/s]

The alexnet model is split up into two components: alexnet.features and alexnet.classifier. The first neural network component, alexnet.features, is used to compute convolutional features, which are taken as input in alexnet.classifier.

The neural network alexnet.features expects an image tensor of shape Nx3x224x224 as input and it will output a tensor of shape Nx256x6x6 . (N = batch size).

Compute the AlexNet features for each of your training, validation, and test data. Here is an example code snippet showing how you can compute the AlexNet features for some images (your actual code might be different):

In [ ]:
features = alexnet.features
IM_MEAN = torch.tensor([0.485, 0.456, 0.406]).view(1,3,1,1)
IM_STD  = torch.tensor([0.229, 0.224, 0.225]).view(1,3,1,1)

def get_fea(loader):
  xs, ys = [], []

  with torch.no_grad():
    for x, y1h in loader:                       # x: [N, 3, 224, 224] in [0, 1]
      x = (x - IM_MEAN) / IM_STD                # image norm
      f = features(x).view(x.size(0), -1)       # f: [N, 256, 6, 6] -> [N, 256*6*6]

      xs.append(f)
      ys.append(y1h.argmax(1))

  return torch.cat(xs), torch.cat(ys)


# feature computation
x_train_features, y_train = get_fea(train_loader)
x_val_features, y_val = get_fea(val_loader)
x_test_features, y_test = get_fea(test_loader)

Save the computed features. You will be using these features as input to your neural network in Part (ii), and you do not want to re-compute the features every time. Instead, run alexnet.features once for each image, and save the result.

In [ ]:
# saved computed features
torch.save({"X": x_train_features, "y": y_train, "classes": classes}, "train_feats.pt")
torch.save({"X": x_val_features, "y": y_val, "classes": classes}, "val_feats.pt")
torch.save({"X": x_test_features, "y": y_test, "classes": classes}, "test_feats.pt")

Part (ii) - [2pt MODEL]¶

Build a new classifier to attach to the AlexNet feature extractor. Your model must use the following sequence of layers:

AlexNet feature → Flatten → Linear → ReLU → Dropout → Linear

Use a dropout probability of 20%; this value can be tuned in the next part. Justify your choice of the Linear layer sizes.

Here is an example of how your model may be called:

In [ ]:
# features = ... load precomputed alexnet.features(img) ...
# output = model(features)
# prob = F.softmax(output)
In [ ]:
# Fully-connected layer

class AlexNetClassifier(nn.Module):
  def __init__(self, p=0.2):
    super(AlexNetClassifier, self).__init__()
    self.fc1 = nn.Linear(256*6*6, 32)
    self.fc2 = nn.Linear(32, 9)
    self.dp = nn.Dropout(p)

  def forward(self, x):
    x = self.dp(F.relu(self.fc1(x)))    # already flatten feature in saved feature in part (i)
    logits = self.fc2(x)                # use Cross Entropy in training, so no softmax here, as CE will include

    return logits
In [ ]:
'''
I select 2 linear layers to prevent overfitting(compared to >2 layers) and converges more stably(compared to 1 layer).
'''

xf_val_loader = DataLoader(TensorDataset(x_val, y_val), batch_size=BATCH_SIZE, generator=g, shuffle=False)

In [ ]:
def get_accuracy(net, loader):
  net.eval()

  correct, total = 0, 0

  with torch.no_grad():
    for xf, label in loader:
      pred = net(xf).argmax(1)

      correct += (label==pred).sum().item()
      total += label.size(0)


  return correct / total
In [ ]:
# TO BE COMPLETED
def train_alex(net, loader, lr=1e-3, wd=0, dp=0.2,
               batch_size=BATCH_SIZE, num_epochs=20):

  # net = AlexNetClassifier(p=dp)
  criterion = nn.CrossEntropyLoss(reduction='mean')
  optimizer = optim.SGD(net.parameters(), lr=0.01, momentum=0.9)

  iters, losses, train_acc, validation_acc = [], [], [], []
  step = 1

  # training
  for epoch in range(num_epochs):
    net.train()
    for xf, label in loader:

      optimizer.zero_grad()
      logits = net(xf)
      loss = criterion(logits, label)
      loss.backward()
      optimizer.step()

      step+=1

      iters.append(step)
      losses.append(loss.item())

    tr_acc = get_accuracy(net, xf_train_loader)
    val_acc = get_accuracy(net, xf_val_loader)
    train_acc.append(tr_acc)
    validation_acc.append(val_acc)
    print(f"Epoch {epoch+1:02d} | train_acc={tr_acc:.4f} | val_acc={val_acc:.4f} | last_loss={losses[-1]:.4f}")


  # plotting
  plt.title("Training Curve")
  plt.plot(iters, losses, label="Train")
  plt.xlabel("Iterations")
  plt.ylabel("Loss")
  plt.show()

  epochs = list(range(1, len(train_acc)+1))
  plt.title("Training Accuracy")
  plt.plot(epochs, train_acc, label="Train")
  plt.plot(epochs, validation_acc, label="Validation")
  plt.xlabel("Epochs")
  plt.ylabel("Accuracy")
  plt.legend(loc='best')
  plt.show()


  return iters, losses, train_acc, validation_acc, net

xf_my_loader = DataLoader(TensorDataset(x_my, y_my), batch_size=BATCH_SIZE, generator=g, shuffle=True)

PART C (Optional) - Bonus Challenge!¶

This is an optional exercise for those that finish the assignment early and would like to take on some additional challenging task.

For this bonus challenge you are asked to explore different techniques to further improve the model for more realistic scenarios where the hands may be in front of various backgrounds, be taken at different scales, rotations, and positions in the image. To build a superior image classification model you can complete one or all of the following tasks.

Tasks:

  1. Test your best models (with or without transfer learning) on hand gestures images with backgrounds that are not clean and smooth. You can take your own hand gesture images, or find ones online to test your model. Comment on the performance of your model.
  2. Generated additional data by performing data augmentation to replace the clean, smooth backgrounds with backgrounds with different textures. Do this on all your training, validation, and test data. This task can be done manually (could take a long time) or you can implement code that can automate the task. For Example, one approach you could take to automate this task is to use pretrained image segmentation tools to identify the hands in the images and crop them out and put them onto other backgrounds.
  3. Improve on your data augmentation by applying scale, rotation, and translation transformations on different backgrounds.
  4. Compare the performance of your best CNN models (with and without transfoer learning) trained with data augmentation to the results in 1. where you did not train on images with data augmentation.
  5. Implement one of many region proposal tools to detect hand gestures in image frames and put a bounding box around the region with the highest confidence. You can use pretrained YOLO models, or a region proposal tool from openCV.
  6. Create a short video demonstration how you can use your hand gesture recognition model to communicate a message using hand gestures.

Bonus marks will be provided based on the number of steps completed. Summarize below your results and anything intersting you learned from the steps that you completed. Bonus marks cannot be accumulated beyond the maximum assignment grade.

# ======== part 1: Unzip and save the anonymized data files ========

ZIP_PATH_new = "/content/archive.zip"
DATA_ROOT_new = Path("/content/kaggle_data")


seed = 999
BATCH_SIZE = 64


if DATA_ROOT_new.exists():
    shutil.rmtree(DATA_ROOT_new)
DATA_ROOT_new.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

with zipfile.ZipFile(ZIP_PATH_new, "r") as z:
    z.extractall(DATA_ROOT_new)


# ======== part 2: read images & create claesses ========

samples_new = []
for p in DATA_ROOT_new.glob("*/*/*/*.jpg"):
    cls = p.parent.name
    samples_new.append((p, cls))


# create classes
classes_new = sorted({c for _, c in samples_new})
class_to_idx_new = {c: i for i, c in enumerate(classes_new)}


# ======== part 3: Transformation ========

new_ds = ASLDataset(samples_new, classes_new, class_to_idx_new)
new_loader = DataLoader(new_ds, batch_size=BATCH_SIZE, shuffle=False)

Assignment Grading Rubric¶
The grading of the assignment will be based on the following categories:


(0) 5 Pt - DATA Generating new data to evaluate your model.


(1) 9 Pt - EXPLORATORY QUESTIONS These are basic questions that in most cases can be answered without requiring a fully working and trained neural network model. For example, data loading, processing and visualization, summary statistics, data exploration, model and training setup, etc.


(2) 9 Pt - MODEL Student has successfully implemented all the required neural network models and has demonstrated successful training of the model without any errors.


(3) 9 Pt - RESULT Students are evaluated based on the results achieved in comparison to the expected results of the assignment.


(4) 9 Pt - DISCUSSION QUESTIONS Student demonstrated understanding beyond the basic exploratory questions, can answer some of the more challenging questions, and provide arguments for their model selection decisions.


(5) 9 Pt - COMMUNICATION Student has provided a quality submission that is easy to read without too many unnecessary output statements that distract the reading of the document. The code has been well commented and all the answers are communicated clearly and concisely.


(6) 5 Pt - BONUS Student has completed the assignment and has taken on the challenging bonus tasks listed in PART C. The student has demonstrated a good understanding of all aspects of the assignment and has exceeded expectations for the assignment.
